newsitem.title: UK: Christmas sales edge up at Laura Ashley. [CORRECTED 08:48 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Christmas sales edge up at Laura Ashley. [CORRECTED 08:48 GMT]

text.p: UK textiles and furniture group Laura Ashley Holdings Plc said on Tuesday that its total like-for-like retail sales in the six weeks from November 24, 1996 to January 4 rose by 3.0 percent, bolstered by a strong performance in the British retail market, .
In a statement the company added that for the longer period of 23 weeks starting from July 28, 1996 to January 4 like-for-like sales rose by 1.0 percent.

The company said that the sales breakdown showed a clear dip in North American sales in the autumn of last year on both a total and like-for-like basis and this reflected the closure of 19 shops. However, a recovery fed through over Christmas when the region's like-for-like sales rose by 1.0 percent
"The new shops, another 12 of which opened in the fourth quarter, are beginning to show top line growth and contributed to the improved performance in the six week christmas period."
Foreign exchange movements positively affected sales in North America by 1.0 percent, Laura Ashley added.

In continental Europe Christmas sales were lower than in the same 1995 period at both total and like-for-like levels, though for the longer 23 week trading period like-for-like sales fell by 9.0 percent (company corrects from "showed a small 1.0 percent rise").
The company said sales were adversely affected "by difficult trading conditions generally and a five percent foreign exchange impact".

Chief executive Ann Iverson was quoted as saying "I am pleased with recent sales performance, both in the UK and particularly North America. We remain fully on track for this financial year and for 1997/98."
